Messages.Author: Todd Banister
Messages.Body:
Question: Why does a strike with first strike not beat a dodge or S:CE? I
understand that the VTES rulebook states this very clearly that they (dodge
and S:CE) beat the first strike. No arguments that the rulebook stated
that. But the rulebook leaves a lot to be desired in my opinion.

What I do argue is that under First Strike (page 29 or 50 I can't
remember), it also says that a strike with first strike resolves before the
regular strike occur. If the strike resolves before other strikes occur
(and that would be when the S:CE and dodge happen) why would the dodge and
s:ce go back and override that? This just does not make any sense to me. I
did read in the Deja News archives that dodge would cancel a strike that
was played before or after the dodge was played. Why? Forget the rulings
for a second, If I smacked you with first strike and caused damage to you
and you were not able to prevent it, how could you then go back and dodge
it? Same thing with S:CE. I think that the first strike should resolve and
then S:CE could be played in the other players normal strike phase and the
S:CE would cancel the rest of combat. I do not believe that letting first
strike resolve before dodge and S:CE would unbalance the game in any way.
If anything, it would help out by giving a way around the S:CE abuse that
you see (at least in my playgroup). Its not like first strike will change
the face that combat decks (in general) do not do well at all in tournament
play either.

Any help on this would be great.
TB

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Todd Banister wrote:
>
> Question: Why does a strike with first strike not beat a dodge or S:CE? I
> understand that the VTES rulebook states this very clearly that they (dodge
> and S:CE) beat the first strike. No arguments that the rulebook stated
> that. But the rulebook leaves a lot to be desired in my opinion.
>
> What I do argue is that under First Strike (page 29 or 50 I can't
> remember), it also says that a strike with first strike resolves before the
> regular strike occur. If the strike resolves before other strikes occur
> (and that would be when the S:CE and dodge happen)

No. Strike: Comabt Ends and Strike: Dodge are not regular strikes.
They are special strikes.

Strike: Comabt Ends ends combat at the start of strike resolution.
Strike: Dodge cancel any effect the opposing strike has on the Dodging
minion and any non-Retainer cards on him.

If you like, Dodge doesn't resolve first - but it does retroactively
cancel the effects of the opposing strike.

So, you might as well say that it resolves first, to avoid confusion.

why would the dodge and
> s:ce go back and override that? This just does not make any sense to me. I
> did read in the Deja News archives that dodge would cancel a strike that
> was played before or after the dodge was played. Why? Forget the rulings
> for a second, If I smacked you with first strike and caused damage to you
> and you were not able to prevent it, how could you then go back and dodge
> it?

You dodge it. The strike misses. That it was done with First Strike is
immaterial - you dodged it faster.

Strikes are declared (played) in one order (acting player first), then
resolve according to the nature of the strike: S:CE first (since
it resolves at the start of the resolution step, ending the whole step),
then Dodge (since it mostly cancels the opposing strike and this timing
makes it easier to follow), then any other strike done with First Strike
(for obvious reasons), then any other strike (to catch the rest).

> Same thing with S:CE. I think that the first strike should resolve and
> then S:CE could be played in the other players normal strike phase and the
> S:CE would cancel the rest of combat. I do not believe that letting first
> strike resolve before dodge and S:CE would unbalance the game in any way.

It is balance - it's just the WayThingsAre.
Leaving it this way doesn't unbalance the game, either.

--

Messages.Author: Lupus Australis
Messages.Body:
On Mon, 5 Jan 1998 T_Ban...@Premier-Lending.com wrote:

> Is there any way around Thoughts Betrayed? I assume the answer is no.

Well, one could always ban the thing, or make a house rule that it only
works against younger vampires. But even without such laudable measures
one is not completely helpless.

Certain Master Out-Of-Turn cards may be played in combat.

Direct Invervention: A rare Sabbat master card which allows one to cancel
the effects of any one opposing minion card. It's main disadvantage is
that it is a rare Sabbat card (I don't have one either). Also, it does
not prevent ones opponent from playing a second TB if he has one, whereas
you are unlikely to be able to play a second Master-OOT.

Rotschreck: Allows one to put those Lasombra/Giovanni scumbags in torpor
if they attempt to do aggravated damage, which is probably their intent.
One disadvantage is that it does not work against environmental damage.
Another is that it is often banned on account of its confusing text (which
required extensive errata). I'm not sure if it is still banned in
tournament play.

Frenzy: It is unlikely that this card will do you any good whatsoever,
but, since it is a master, you COULD play it after TB "before range is
chosen". Prevents your opponents from relying on equipment or pressing to
end combat, neither of which he is likely planning to do. It also gives
the combat an automatic press, which is probably the last thing you need.
Still, with enough permanents in play, like maybe Spawning Pool....

Problem with all the above cards is that they do not work on your turn, so
are no help if you are blocked, etc.

Those superior Dominators tend to belong to a specific clan, so you could
use clan hosers. Cultivated Blood Shortage will tend to ensure that
Ventrue have insufficient blood to play TB. Malkavian Derangement or
Malkavian Dementia could be useful against Malkavians. In the unlikely
event that your opposing Thought Betrayers happen to be Brujah (Constanza
Vinti and Donal O'Connor come to mind), you could play Brujah Frenzy when
they try to rush you, and sent them elsewhere.

Play Sudden Reversal when they try to put superior Dominate on their
vamps.

Memories of Mortality can make one thought betrayers vulnerable to
attack by allies, since any damage he inflicts on them will be reduced to
0. This only lasts til his next influence phase, but then he is forced to
burn a blood or go into torpor. Since TB costs 2 pool, anything that
forces them to burn blood is a good thing.

Play Millicent Smith. Then block his actions when he controls her.

Certain minion cards, played outside of combat, give effects that will be
useful in combat. For instance: Block with Guard Dogs and you have an
optional maneuver, block with Rat's Warning and you have an optional
press. Precognition allows you to prevent 1 damage and Spirits touch
gives an optional maneuver. Alacrity gives an optional maneuver. Veiled
sight allows one to steal one blood from the opposing minion as a strike.
Mind Tricks gives an optional press or maneuver. Dawn Operation makes all
damage in the resulting combat aggravated, and at superior, your opponent
cannot back out. Eyes of the Night also gives a maneuver or press.
Most important is Uncontrollable Rage. Rush them with this card, and hope
they don't have a dodge.

Kiss of Ra is useful in case those TBers attempt to block you. The main
disadvantage of this card is that it is considered almost as cheesy as TB
itself.

Burn his blood so he does not have enough to use TB. Jar the Soul and
Cryptic Mission are particularly useful here. I have a cryptic mission
deck that would probably hose most TB decks. It also uses Seeds of
Corruption, which would cause them to burn 2 blood with every action.

Fast Reaction and Hidden Lurker can get you into combat with these suckers
when they don't expect it, preventing them from playing strikes, and
starts a new combat just after, most likely, they have already used TB.
They are not prevented from playing another TB, however [though I think
they should be--see seperate post].

Serpentis can be useful against these suckers. Put a Mark of Damnation
upon them and then assault them with hordes of weenies. You can also
tempt them, corrupt them and inflict phobias upon them. Heart of darkness
can be useful for surviving their attacks.

Reliance on permanents is of course the main strategy against these
jokers. Elesium is extremely important. Its fun to tap it to end combat
immediately after they burn 2 blood. You can always go after them with a
Rengade Garou equipped with a Bang Nakh, a Sengir Dagger, a Flak Jacket,
a Leather Jacket, and a Ghoul Retainer. Of course, your opponent, who
has superior dominate, is only going to steal him with Far Mastery before
you are done equipping.

Lupus Australis

As Lupus wrote: the key is: have the right permanents.

The only (reaction) card to counter TB I missed in his list is Obediance
(card text: is about to enter combat, card text of TB: played before
combat), but you need Dominate yourself.

Another location you may use is Living Manse (Tzimisce) to end combat.

The best defense is in my opinion to have some small, expandable vamps /
allies
to block those Dominators so that the use of TB is not justified any
more by its effect. Gangrel Antitribu may laugh at TB when they have one
or two Shadow Court Satyr active, both with Earth Meld to end combat...

Another "defense" may be the vote "Anathema" as some kind of insurance.
The moment your key vamp is reduced to 0 blood he is burned (that's what
your enemy intended anyway) but you get his cost in pool repayed. So you
can get his second copy out at 0 cost (that your enemy did not intend :)

Last thing is: TB costs blood. Use "Banishment".
